title: A Kitchen Measures What Comes Back
transcript:
The kitchen at a community lunch centre has reduced food waste after studying what diners leave on their plates. For two weeks, staff collected leftovers in separate containers for vegetables, potatoes, and other food. They weighed each container at the end of lunch and wrote down which dishes had been served. The results surprised them. The least popular food was not the dish that received the most complaints.

Many diners said the boiled carrots were unexciting, but most ate them. Far more potatoes were left behind, even on days when people praised the meal. Staff discovered that the standard serving was too large for several older customers, who felt uncomfortable asking for less while others waited behind them.

The centre now offers a smaller first serving, with extra food available at no additional charge. Signs explain the arrangement before customers reach the counter, so nobody has to make a special request in front of a queue. The kitchen also places vegetables and potatoes in separate serving dishes, allowing people to choose their own balance.

The centre has not reduced the amount of fresh food it buys simply to claim a saving. Instead, staff compare leftovers with the number of meals served each day. They will repeat the measurements when the winter menu begins, since heavier dishes may produce a different pattern. Customers can still leave comments, but those comments are now considered alongside the kitchen records.

questions.prompt: What did kitchen staff do during the initial study?
options: Asked customers to cook their own meals.
Removed every unpopular dish from the menu.
Separated and weighed different kinds of leftovers.
questions.answer: Separated and weighed different kinds of leftovers.
questions.explanation: 工作人员把剩菜按种类收集，午餐结束后分别称重并记录当天菜品。

questions.prompt: Why did some diners leave many potatoes?
options: The standard serving was too large for them.
They disliked the new cooking method.
The potatoes were served after the meal.
They had to pay extra for vegetables.
questions.answer: The standard serving was too large for them.
questions.explanation: 调查发现统一份量对部分老年顾客过大，而他们又不愿当众要求少盛。

questions.prompt: What is different about the new serving arrangement?
options: Only regular customers may request more food.
A smaller first serving can be followed by free extra food.
Customers must book their portions the day before.
Potatoes and vegetables are always mixed together.
questions.answer: A smaller first serving can be followed by free extra food.
questions.explanation: 现在先提供较小份量，需要时可以免费添餐。

questions.prompt: How will staff make their waste figures more useful?
options: By ignoring comments about unpopular dishes.
By recording only the busiest lunch periods.
By comparing leftovers with the number of meals served.
By buying less fresh food regardless of demand.
questions.answer: By comparing leftovers with the number of meals served.
questions.explanation: 工作人员把剩余量与当天供餐数对照，避免仅凭总重量误判。
